tldr: The second moment of a common-rank indirect conditional-mean attribution retains a nonlocal response product at two mediator quantiles. Its original-record minimax MSE is \(n^{-2\alpha}\) for \(\alpha<1/2\), \(\min\{1,\log(en)^2/n\}\) at \(\alpha=1/2\), and \(n^{-1}\) for \(\alpha>1/2\). A finite crossed-bin empirical-rank estimator attains these orders on the entire declared model. The matching normalized density-only converse keeps one identical control response across its two testing laws in every regime, including a fixed-frequency regular branch. Supplying both densities instead gives \(n^{-\min\{1,8\alpha/(4\alpha+1)\}}\). The two risks have equal orders exactly when \(\alpha>1/2\); otherwise learning mediator ranks has the evaluated polynomial or critical logarithmic price. This is a prospective precision benchmark for one continuous mediator under randomized treatment, without a COMPAS model-fit claim.
